title: Prototype model-variant synthesis + quant tradeoffs (customer workshop notes)
content:
Context and goal:
Small-customer POC (fintech KYC assistant) — goal is to evaluate model variants and quantization modes to hit 95th-pct latency < 200ms on p99 token generation for short prompts (<=120 tokens) while keeping coherent extraction quality for entity-level recall > 90% on our benchmark set. Customer constraints: private deployment in VPC, limited GPU budget (2x A10 or equivalent), cannot accept >10% dropped entities compared to baseline full-fp16.

This doc captures workshop notes, microbenchmarks, quick heuristics we tried, and recommended default pipeline for demo + steps for a follow-up lab.

High-level experiment matrix (ran 2024-11-10 to 2024-11-24):
- Models tested: open-llama-13b, llama2-13b, redwood/opt-14b-slim (internal verified runner), mosaic-7b-instruct-2.0 (baseline for token-efficiency).
- Variants per model: full-fp16, 8-bit dynamic (int8), 4-bit quant (nf4 via bitsandbytes), 4-bit QAT-like (experimental PTQ with small calibration set), hybrid-quant (KV cache fp16 + attention compute 4-bit).
- Prompt types: few-shot extraction template (3 examples), single-shot instruction, chain-of-thought freeform (for debugging only).
- Evaluation workloads: 120 short KYC forms, 500 synthetic blanks for latency measurements (no heavy I/O), 40 adversarial forms for recall stress test.

Key observations (summary):
1) Latency vs quality sweet spot: For this workload, 8-bit dynamic hits ~75–85% of the fp16 quality with ~1.6x speedup in token throughput. 4-bit PTQ improves throughput 2.6–3.2x but shows inconsistent entity boundaries (tokenization drift) on ~8% of samples. Hybrid-quant (only KV in fp16) reduces that drift to ~3–4% while still giving ~2.2x speedup.

2) Cache and prefix heuristics matter: Because many KYC prompts share canonical prefixes (prompt header + instructions), enabling prefix caching at the runtime layer reduced end-to-end latency by ~18–24% for burst traffic. Continuous batching at small window sizes (10–15ms) preserved p99 while improving GPU utilization for 8-bit/4-bit.

3) Tokenization sanity checks: Some 4-bit quant variants amplified tokenizer mismatch effects (rare unicode or long-emoji fields). Add a pre-tokenization normalization step (NFKC, collapse repeated whitespace) in pipeline to reduce spurious entity splits.

4) Canary routing: For demo, route 10% of requests to fp16 fallback path and 90% to quant variant; automatic fallback on confidence/partial parse failure preserved customer-facing correctness while showing latency gains.

Microbenchmark snippets (numbers averaged across 5 runs, 2xA10):
- open-llama-13b fp16: mean token-latency 11.4ms, p95 token-latency 24ms, decode throughput ~420 tok/s. Entity F1: 0.92.
- open-llama-13b int8: mean token-latency 7.6ms, p95 17ms, throughput ~620 tok/s. Entity F1: 0.86.
- open-llama-13b 4-bit PTQ: mean token-latency 4.3ms, p95 9.8ms, throughput ~980 tok/s. Entity F1: 0.84 (but recall drop concentrated on hyphenated names).
- open-llama-13b hybrid-4b (KV fp16): mean token-latency 5.1ms, p95 12ms, throughput ~820 tok/s. Entity F1: 0.90.

Practical tuning notes (what we changed during workshop):
- Quant calibration: used a 512-example calibration corpus sampled from customer anonymized forms. For 4-bit PTQ, limiting calibration to representative short-context examples improved entity preservation. Avoid long-tail out-of-distribution examples in calibration set.
- Attention kernel selection: pin to Triton kernels that are optimized for sequence length <= 128. Benchmarked alternative kernels; some graph compilation choices changed p95 by up to 10ms. Keep kernel-selection config documented with model variant.
- KV cache layout: store KV in fp16; keep compute in quantized form where supported. This gave most of the quality benefits at moderate cost.
- Batch size policy: dynamic batch window of 12ms default, max batch size 8 for 13B variants; higher batch sizes increase throughput but p95 suffers for 90th+ percentile requests.

Prompt/pipeline tuning (quick recipes):
- Use short canonical instruction header (<= 3 sentences) then a single-shot example template. Longer few-shot examples improved extraction by ~2–3% F1 but added steady-state token cost and latency for every call — tradeoff discussed with customer.
- Post-processing: deterministic entity normalization rules (strip punctuation, standardize whitespace) reduced false negatives from tokenization drift. Add regex-based catches for hyphen and diacritics.
- Confidence scoring heuristic: compute span confidence via token-logprob average and fallback to fp16 route if avg logprob < threshold (-2.5 empirically). Also trigger fallback when parse returns fewer than expected number of fields.

Deployment proposal for POC/demo (recommended):
1) Deploy hybrid-4b variant as default serving image behind Redwood runtime with prefix caching enabled.
2) Canary policy: 10% fp16 fallback route + automatic fallback on low-confidence parse.
3) Autoscaling: reserve 2xA10 for baseline; set burst capacity to 1 extra node for demo spikes.
4) Observability: add a per-request tag for quant-mode, log token-level latencies, and track entity-level F1 over time. Run daily small-eval to detect regressions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Edge cases in tokenization (names with emojis/rare punctuation): mitigation = pre-normalization + deterministic post-normalization + escalate to fp16 when unknown-token rate > 2%.
- Calibration drift when customer dataset shifts: schedule weekly recalibration job that samples new anonymized forms and re-run PTQ calibration (automated job in CI).
- Reproducibility across hardware: 4-bit behavior differs by GPU architecture/drivers — lock to supported driver versions and include a hardware-compatibility matrix in deployment docs.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Try QAT-like fine-tuning for 4-bit on a small labeled subset (200 examples) to see if entity-level recall reaches parity with fp16. (cost estimate: ~6–8 GPU-hours on one A100).
- Investigate attention-kernel compile flags that caused the p95 regression for longer sequences (seen in one build). Raise with runtime team (ticket attached).
- Evaluate hybrid routing where certain prompt types (forms with >6 fields) automatically route to fp16 by content classifier.

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: spin up reproducible lab run for hybrid-4b + calibration (due 2024-11-30) — include exact Dockerfile and kernel flags.
- Elena: add token normalization and post-processing module to the pipeline repo, include regex sets for hyphens/diacritics (due 2024-12-06).
- Samir: wire up per-route observability dashboards and drift alert (entity-F1 delta > 3%) (due 2024-12-10).
- Maya: prepare POC deck for customer showing tradeoffs and recommended default (due 2024-12-05).

Appendix: quick checklist for repeating the run
- dataset: customer-kvc-2024-anon-512-calib.csv (sampled)
- kernel flags: TRITON_SEQ<=128, USE_BF16=false, ENABLE_FUSED_ATTENTION=true
- quant stack: bitsandbytes v0.39 + patched loader for nf4; calibration script: quant_calib_v2.py --sample 512 --seed 42
- prompt template sample: "INSTRUCTIONS: Extract fields: name, dob, id_number. Example:
Input: [FORM]
Output: {name: "Ana-Marie Cruz", dob: "1989-05-02", id_number: "X1234567"}"

Notes to self (workshop friction items):
- Need a clearer way to pin kernel choices per model in deployment config (current runtime flags are global).
- Customer asked for offline quality audit report — prepare summary with representative failure cases (3–5 examples) and remediation steps.

End of notes.
